He wasn't born with a cork either. Nobody is. You just stand in the right place while you're scared. That's all it ever was.
But I remember now — before every tourney, he'd go very quiet and rub his thumb on his sword-hilt till it shone. I thought it was for luck.
It wasn't luck. He was scared. He did it anyway. That's all it ever was.
So you're going to be scared tomorrow.
Magnificently. I shall be the most frightened man ever to stand in front of a god. And I shall stand there.
Someone should carve that on my tomb. Not soon. Ideally never.
Tomorrow is my birthday. I am practicing being older. How am I doing?
Ilse measured me. Against the galley door on the Halcyon.
And?
Half an inch. Since the Kindling, I have grown half an inch.
In Evernoon I would be sixteen forever. Never older. Never anything.
I want the other halves. All of the inches. I want gray hair. Corvin has some. He says it is terrible. I think it is the best thing I have ever seen.
Don't tell him that.
I told him. He went very quiet and gave me his hat.
I do not have a birthday. Lysa had one, in spring. I do not want hers.
Then pick one.
Tomorrow.
If there is a tomorrow, that is my birthday. And if there is not... then I had a very short life, and it was mine.
There's going to be a tomorrow, Sable.
Then you owe me a present.
If you tell anyone I said "it was great," I'm stealing your boots. Both of 'em. While you're wearing 'em.
Don't make it a whole thing.
I didn't say anything.
You were gonna. You've got your whole-thing face on.
I don't know how to stop. Being the oldest. Corvin keeps doing stuff FOR me. Ilse cut my hair. Bram carries me to my hammock when I fall asleep on deck, like a sack of flour.
And I LIKED it, okay? It was GREAT. I'm gonna be so embarrassed about this later.
When this is done... can I still be on the crew? Even if I'm, like, twelve? Just twelve? Doing twelve stuff?
Pip. You can be twelve as long as you want.
Don't tell Corvin I said any of this. He'll do the hair-ruffle thing.
Watch is mine tonight. Strange feeling, staying put. I could get used to it.
Pull up a crate, sparrow. The good crate. I've been saving it.
Want to know something funny? Every bone in my body's been telling me to run since the desert. Loud. Persistent. Very good arguments.
And I keep not listening. Twelve years I listened to nothing but that voice. Turns out it's a lot less convincing when there's somebody to stay for.
You owed Cassian your life. You said so once.
Pulled me out of a burning barracks when I was nineteen. Never asked for anything back.
Until he asked for everything. Funny how that goes.
You kids went and made me into somebody's — I don't know. Uncle. Bad uncle. The one who teaches you cards and gets you tipsy at weddings.
Corvin.
Mm?
You're not our uncle.
Go on. Get some rest. I'll keep watch. Somebody has to, and I've finally got the knack of it.
Evernoon

The top of the Grand Lantern. There is no roof. There is only the sky — white, enormous — and in the middle of it, the sun.
Not whole. Seven-tenths of it, cracked like an eggshell, held perfectly still by a song nobody can hear anymore.
Beneath it, on the steps of a marble throne, a man in white sits with his hands folded, waiting. He has been waiting a long time. He does not seem to mind.
Face Cassian at the Noon Throne.
Wren. You came all the way up. I'm so glad.
And Sable. You look well. Taller, I think.
Half an inch.
_(smiling)_ So you have.
Did you meet him? Down there? The boy?
He said to tell you he's sorry he was eating honeycake.
For one moment, the Hierophant's face does something complicated. Then it smooths over, like water.
It wasn't anyone's. That's the worst part. It wasn't anyone's fault, and it happened anyway.
Yes. That is the worst part. That is exactly why it must never happen again.
